answer: Inter-arrival timing fingerprinting. A node’s kernel timestamps each identity’s first actions and flags accounts whose traffic curves match a shared scheduler, since clones burst in tight, low-variance gaps no organic user produces. Every identity must then pass a violet-marked probation window with human-scale jitter before its requests count, and spoofing that jitter costs an attacker per-identity compute and delay that scales with fleet size. The signal is the gap distribution itself, so mass registration pays in wall-clock time rather than fees.
